projects.title: No Art FPS
projects.summary: A bright low-poly FPS in 60-second rounds: bold colors, comic outlines and escalating feedback make a compact, satisfying experience.
contributions: Make style serve play：Built a bright low-poly world in sand, cream and cobalt blue, unifying original graffiti, comic outlines, the weapon and a minimal HUD. A visible magazine conveys ammunition so attention stays in the scene.

Pack the action into 60 seconds：Shaped short rounds with three stages of increasing enemies, kill-streak feedback and quick restarts. The final 15 seconds enter DESTROY, followed by an arena blast in the last second: a clear build-up and finish.

Iterate around the experience：Iterated on the loading-to-start transition, per-shot feedback, enemy obstacle avoidance and connected stairs. Combined Godot / GDScript with editable Blender modules, using Codex to connect gameplay, art and browser delivery.
projects.ownership: I define the gameplay goals, visual direction and experience trade-offs, collaborating with Codex on development and iteration.

projects.title: Brushline Rally
projects.summary: From a driving prototype to a playable offline rally game, bringing driving feel, visual design and releases into one iterative process.
contributions: Break down the goal: validate the driving prototype first, then expand tracks, cars and challenges. Use staged milestones so every step produces something playable.
Choose the technology: use Godot, GDScript and Jolt with 120 Hz physics, tire and suspension models, balancing realism with control.
Unify the design: compare art directions and choose a screenprint style, connecting Blender assets, track environments, menus and HUD into a consistent visual language.
Iterate with evidence: use input replays, vehicle telemetry and regression scenarios to validate driving aids and performance, then deliver demo builds and recordings.
projects.ownership: I led product direction, technology choices, visual design and validation, collaborating with Codex on development.

projects.title: Photo Museum
projects.summary: Turn a personal photo library into an explorable exhibition, from local search and event organization to spatial browsing and AI curation.
contributions: Define the boundaries: start with real photo-management needs, keep NAS access read-only, run recognition locally and load originals on demand. Include privacy, caching and running costs in the design.

Assign responsibilities: use a Python API and workers, React and SQLite. Local search and recognition provide facts; a tool-constrained AI assistant curates exhibitions without unrestricted library access.

Make the experience tangible: evolve concepts into Cover Flow, calendars, maps and spatial galleries, then add everyday search and representative selections so photos are both enjoyable and easy to find.
Close the feedback loop: use blind aesthetic comparisons, reversible identity confirmation, interaction regressions and screen recordings to improve loading, cancellation and gestures.
projects.ownership: I led requirements, architecture decisions, interaction design and validation, collaborating with Codex on development.

projects.title: Nex Vibe Coding Platform
projects.summary: Turn natural-language requests into working websites and applications.
contributions: Led the evolution of the Nex Agent protocol from plain-text SSE and XML commands to native tool calls and WebSocket RPC, covering the agent, frontend consumers, unit tests and removal of the legacy protocol.
Designed Prechat/Postchat routing and Plan, Todo and askUser collaboration, using structured outputs, deterministic gates and completion checks to make complex tasks more controllable.
Evolved Subagents into an orchestrator built on planners, workers and a graph state machine, with layered gates, token budgets, pause/resume, reconnection, persistence and task visualization.
Built context-window management with hot/warm-zone compression, dynamic budgets, tool-message pairing, usage visualization and automatic compression and retry after overflow.

Established four layers of tool-execution reliability: frontend/backend timeouts, a serial shell queue, WebSocket circuit breaking and WebContainer health checks; addressed interrupted streams, concurrent writes and auto-repair races.
Built end-to-end agent diagnostics and telemetry from scratch, connecting quality events, tracing, error analysis, monthly token reports and operational views for session-level diagnosis.

projects.title: PGOS Multiplayer Backend
projects.summary: Match players, form teams and host dedicated game servers.
contributions: Contributed to PGOS since 2021, covering competitor research, technology selection, project initiation, core development and launch.
Developed core services for game sessions, matchmaking and persistent connections, supporting rule-based teams, competitive matchmaking and session allocation.

Built configurable matchmaking with declarative rulesets and an expression engine to describe player attributes, team structures and multidimensional constraints, reducing repeated implementation across games.
Designed for fairness, search efficiency and queue time, with rules that relax as players wait, multiple matching modes and concurrent rulesets.
Helped build the matching platform with composite indexes, priority queues, ticket lifecycle management, a simulator and autoscaling for rule debugging and distributed execution.
Built DS Hosting, a flexible, autoscaling server-fleet management system for dedicated game servers.
Implemented Knative-based Virtual Server clusters so developers could extend PGOS through event-driven services.
